name: Say 'World' before 'War' after a preposition (during, of, in)
description: In 20th-century history prose it promotes "World" (as in World War) after any preposition or verb that places an event in time, across many contexts ("The Spanish–American War and World", "military personnel of World", "the Ottoman Empire in World", "From The Romans To The Second World"). Ablated, the model prefers "the" or another proper noun ("War and Philippine" at p ≈ 0.45, "personnel of the" at p ≈ 0.93).
